```text
package spi

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"log/slog"
	"sync/atomic"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
)

// CheckResult contains the result of a provider check operation
type CheckResult struct {
	Success      bool   // Whether the check succeeded
	Version      string // Version of the provider (empty on failure)
	Location     string // File path/location of the provider executable or IDE storage
	ErrorType    string // CheckError* classification on failure; empty on success
	ErrorMessage string // Error message if check failed (empty on success)
}

// ProgressCallback reports progress during session parsing/processing
// current: number of items processed so far (1-based)
// total: total number of items to process
type ProgressCallback func(current, total int)

// AgentChatSession represents a chat session from an AI coding agent
type AgentChatSession struct {
	SessionID   string              // Stable and unique identifier for the session (often a UUID)
	CreatedAt   string              // Stable ISO 8601 timestamp when session was created
	Slug        string              // Stable human-readable but file name safe slug, often derived from first user message
	SessionData *schema.SessionData // Structured session data in unified format
	RawData     string              // Raw session data (e.g., JSON blobs for Cursor CLI, JSONL for Claude Code and Codex CLI, etc.)
}

// SessionDataJSON marshals the session's normalized SessionData to a JSON string for
// cloud sync. SessionData is the canonical cloud-resume representation (the cloud
// stores and serves it verbatim), so it is pushed alongside the existing markdown and
// rawData. Returns "" (and logs) when there is no SessionData or marshaling fails, so
// callers can pass the result straight through — an empty payload simply means "no
// cloud-resumable blob for this session" and the server leaves session_data_size NULL.
func (s *AgentChatSession) SessionDataJSON() string {
	if s == nil || s.SessionData == nil {
		return ""
	}
	data, err := json.Marshal(s.SessionData)
	if err != nil {
		slog.Warn("Failed to marshal SessionData for cloud sync", "sessionId", s.SessionID, "error", err)
		return ""
	}
	return string(data)
}

// SessionMetadata contains lightweight metadata about a session without full content
// Used by ListAgentChatSessions for efficient session listing
type SessionMetadata struct {
	SessionID string `json:"session_id" csv:"session_id"` // Stable and unique identifier for the session
	CreatedAt string `json:"created_at" csv:"created_at"` // Stable ISO 8601 timestamp when session was created
	Slug      string `json:"slug" csv:"slug"`             // Stable human-readable session name/slug
	Name      string `json:"name" csv:"name"`             // Human-readable description of the session (may be empty if not available)
}

// GlobalSessionRef is a lightweight, project-discovering reference to a single
// native session, returned by Provider.ListAllAgentChatSessions.
//
// Unlike the project-scoped ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath), the project is NOT
// an input here: each ref carries the originating working directory (read from inside
// the session) so the caller — the `specstory reindex` command — can resolve project
// identity with utils.ComputeProjectID. The project is discovered, not supplied.
//
// It is intentionally metadata-only (no full SessionData parse); reindex re-fetches
// full data per ref via GetAgentChatSession(OriginCwd, SessionID) when it needs the
// conversation body. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
type GlobalSessionRef struct {
	SessionID  string // native session id (uuid)
	CreatedAt  string // ISO 8601 creation timestamp (first turn), may be empty
	Slug       string // filename-safe slug derived from the first user message
	Name       string // human-readable description (may be empty)
	NativePath string // absolute path the provider opens to read this session
	OriginCwd  string // working directory the session was launched from (-> project_id)
}

// ScanReporter accumulates a provider's enumeration progress (sessions found) so the CLI can
// render a live "scanning" display. It is safe for concurrent use and safe to call on a nil
// receiver (a no-op), so providers can report unconditionally.
type ScanReporter struct {
	found atomic.Int64
}

// Add records that n more sessions have been found. Files that yield no session (warmup-only or
// sidechain-only transcripts) are deliberately not counted, so the running total reflects real
// sessions rather than raw files.
func (r *ScanReporter) Add(n int) {
	if r != nil {
		r.found.Add(int64(n))
	}
}

// Found returns the number of sessions found so far.
func (r *ScanReporter) Found() int64 {
	if r == nil {
		return 0
	}
	return r.found.Load()
}

// Provider defines the interface that all agent coding tool providers must implement.
// PathSessionReader and ProgressEnumerator below are optional capabilities.
type Provider interface {
	// Name returns the human-readable name of the provider (e.g., "Claude Code", "Cursor CLI", "Codex CLI")
	Name() string

	// Check verifies if the provider is properly installed and returns version info
	// customCommand: empty string = use detected/default binary path, non-empty = use this specific command/path
	Check(customCommand string) CheckResult

	// DetectAgent checks if the provider's agent has been used in the given project path
	// projectPath: Agent's working directory
	// helpOutput: if true AND no activity is found, the provider should output helpful guidance
	// Returns true if the agent has created artifacts/sessions in the specified path
	DetectAgent(projectPath string, helpOutput bool) bool

	// GetAgentChatSession retrieves a single chat session by ID for the given project path
	// projectPath: Agent's working directory
	// sessionID: specific session identifier to retrieve (always provided, never empty)
	// debugRaw: if true, provider should write provider-specific raw debug files to .specstory/debug/<sessionID>/
	//           (e.g., numbered JSON files). The unified session-data.json is written centrally by the CLI.
	// Returns nil if the session is not found, error for actual errors
	GetAgentChatSession(projectPath string, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*AgentChatSession, error)

	// GetAgentChatSessions retrieves all chat sessions for the given project path
	// projectPath: Agent's working directory
	// debugRaw: if true, provider should write provider-specific raw debug files to .specstory/debug/<sessionID>/
	//           (e.g., numbered JSON files). The unified session-data.json is written centrally by the CLI.
	// progress: optional callback for reporting progress during parsing (nil = no progress reporting)
	// Returns a slice of AgentChatSession structs containing session data
	GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress ProgressCallback) ([]AgentChatSession, error)

	// ListAgentChatSessions retrieves lightweight metadata for all sessions without full parsing
	// This should be faster than GetAgentChatSessions as it only needs to return SessionMetadata and not the full AgentChatSession
	// projectPath: Agent's working directory
	// Returns a slice of SessionMetadata (ordering is provider-defined; consumers will sort if needed)
	ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]SessionMetadata, error)

	// ExecAgentAndWatch executes the agent in interactive mode and watches for session updates
	// Blocks until the agent exits, calling sessionCallback for each new/updated session
	// projectPath: Agent's working directory
	// customCommand: empty string = use detected/default binary with default args, non-empty = use this specific command/path
	// resumeSessionID: empty string = start new session, non-empty = resume this specific session ID
	// debugRaw: if true, provider should write provider-specific raw debug files to .specstory/debug/<sessionID>/
	//           (e.g., numbered JSON files). The unified session-data.json is written centrally by the CLI.
	// sessionCallback is called with each session update. Deliver updates in order,
	// contain callback panics, and finish all callbacks before returning.
	// The implementation should handle its own file watching and session tracking
	ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*AgentChatSession)) error

	// WatchAgent watches for agent activity and calls the callback with an updated AgentChatSession
	// Does NOT execute the agent - only watches for new activity
	// Runs until error or context cancellation
	// ctx: Context for cancellation and timeout control
	// projectPath: Agent's working directory
	// debugRaw: if true, provider should write provider-specific raw debug files to .specstory/debug/<sessionID>/
	//           (e.g., numbered JSON files). The unified session-data.json is written centrally by the CLI.
	// sessionCallback: called with AgentChatSession on each update. Deliver updates
	// in order, contain callback panics, and finish all callbacks before returning.
	// The implementation should handle its own file watching and session tracking
	WatchAgent(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*AgentChatSession)) error

	// ReconstructSession rebuilds the provider's native session format from the
	// neutral SessionData so the agent can resume the conversation (the reverse of
	// the parse/generate path). It is a pure transform: it returns the native file
	// bytes, a freshly minted native-format session ID, and a suggested filename,
	// but does NOT touch the filesystem — writing into the live agent store is the
	// caller's responsibility.
	//
	// Every provider carries this responsibility; providers that do not yet have a
	// native serializer return ErrReconstructionUnsupported.
	// See docs/SESSION-PORTABILITY.md for the design.
	ReconstructSession(data *schema.SessionData, opts ReconstructOptions) (*ReconstructedSession, error)

	// NativeSessionPath resolves the absolute path where a reconstructed session
	// file (with the given base filename, from ReconstructedSession.Filename)
	// belongs in this provider's native store for the given project, WITHOUT
	// requiring the directory to exist — the caller creates it and writes the file.
	// Providers without a native serializer return ErrReconstructionUnsupported.
	NativeSessionPath(projectPath string, filename string) (string, error)

	// SupportsReconstruction reports whether this provider has a native
	// serializer — i.e. whether it can be a cross-agent (or cloud) resume
	// target. It must agree with ReconstructSession/NativeSessionPath returning
	// ErrReconstructionUnsupported, and must be a pure capability answer with no
	// filesystem access: callers invoke it just to build target lists (some
	// NativeSessionPath implementations prepare directories, so probing that is
	// not a substitute).
	SupportsReconstruction() bool

	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every session in this provider's native
	// store, regardless of project — the inverse of the project-scoped
	// ListAgentChatSessions. Each returned ref carries the originating cwd (read from
	// inside the session) so the caller can resolve project identity; the project is
	// discovered, not supplied. Lightweight: metadata only, no full SessionData parse.
	// Used by `specstory reindex` to (re)build the restore index. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
	ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]GlobalSessionRef, error)
}

// Optional provider capabilities. A provider may implement either, both, or
// neither; callers fall back to the required Provider methods when absent.

// PathSessionReader is an OPTIONAL capability a Provider may implement: parse a single
// session directly from its already-known native file path, skipping the by-id discovery
// search that GetAgentChatSession performs.
//
// Why: some providers locate a session by scanning their native store. Codex's by-id
// lookup walks the entire ~/.codex/sessions tree on every call, so resolving N sessions
// that way is O(N²). reindex already holds each session's exact file path
// (GlobalSessionRef.NativePath) from enumeration, so a path-keyed parse turns that back
// into O(N). reindex prefers this when a provider implements it and the ref carries a
// NativePath, and falls back to GetAgentChatSession otherwise.
//
// originCwd is the session's originating working directory (GlobalSessionRef.OriginCwd),
// passed through as the workspace root for path normalization — matching what
// GetAgentChatSession receives as projectPath.
type PathSessionReader interface {
	GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath string, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*AgentChatSession, error)
}

// ProgressEnumerator is an OPTIONAL Provider capability: enumerate all sessions while reporting
// scan progress into r (which may be nil — ScanReporter is nil-safe, so report unconditionally).
// Providers that don't implement it are enumerated via ListAllAgentChatSessions with no live
// feedback. reindex uses this to render a per-agent "Scanning agents…" display.
type ProgressEnumerator interface {
	ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *ScanReporter) ([]GlobalSessionRef, error)
}
```

```text
package cursoride

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"time"

	"github.com/google/uuid"

	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/providers/vscode"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
	"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi/schema"
)

// cursorBubbleTypeUser and cursorBubbleTypeAssistant are the type values Cursor IDE
// uses to distinguish user and assistant bubbles in ComposerConversation rows.
const (
	cursorBubbleTypeUser      = 1
	cursorBubbleTypeAssistant = 2

	// cursorUnifiedModeAgent is the unifiedMode value for Cursor's "Agent" mode.
	// Reconstructed sessions use this mode since cross-provider imports are agent-style.
	cursorUnifiedModeAgent = 2
)

// ReconstructSession rebuilds a Cursor IDE native session from the neutral SessionData
// and writes it directly into the global state.vscdb. Cursor IDE stores all sessions
// as key-value rows in a single shared SQLite database rather than per-session files,
// so the write happens here instead of in the caller's writeReconstructedSession step.
//
// One composerData:* row is written for the session metadata, and one bubbleId:*:* row
// is written per flattened turn. Tool calls and thinking are already collapsed into plain
// text by FlattenSessionData; we store them verbatim in the bubble's Text field.
func (p *Provider) ReconstructSession(data *schema.SessionData, opts spi.ReconstructOptions) (*spi.ReconstructedSession, error) {
	turns, err := spi.PrepareTurns(data, opts)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	globalDbPath, err := GetGlobalDatabasePath()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cursor IDE global database not found: %w", err)
	}

	// Resolve workspace early — we need workspace.ID for the workspaceIdentifier field
	// in composerData, which Cursor uses to associate sessions with their project.
	workspaceRoot := spi.ResolveWorkspaceRoot(opts, data)
	if workspaceRoot == "" {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot register session in Cursor IDE: no workspace root provided")
	}
	// EnsureWorkspaceForProject mints a workspace entry when the folder has never been
	// opened in Cursor, so resuming into a brand-new project works. If even minting
	// fails, tell the user the manual workaround instead of just the raw error.
	workspace, wsErr := EnsureWorkspaceForProject(workspaceRoot)
	if wsErr != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("cannot register session in Cursor IDE (open %q in Cursor once, then retry the resume): %w", workspaceRoot, wsErr)
	}

	newID := uuid.NewString()
	nowMs := time.Now().UnixMilli()

	// Build one bubble per flattened turn.
	bubbles := make([]ComposerConversation, len(turns))
	headers := make([]ComposerConversationHeader, len(turns))
	for i, turn := range turns {
		bubbleID := uuid.NewString()
		bubbleType := cursorBubbleTypeAssistant
		if turn.Role == schema.RoleUser {
			bubbleType = cursorBubbleTypeUser
		}
		tsMs := float64(nowMs + int64(i)*1000)
		createdAt := time.UnixMilli(nowMs + int64(i)*1000).UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano)
		bubbles[i] = ComposerConversation{
			BubbleID:    bubbleID,
			Type:        bubbleType,
			Text:        turn.Text,
			UnifiedMode: cursorUnifiedModeAgent,
			TimingInfo: &TimingInfo{
				ClientStartTime: tsMs,
				ClientEndTime:   tsMs + 500,
			},
		}
		// grouping.isRenderable must be true; without it Cursor skips the bubble entirely.
		headers[i] = ComposerConversationHeader{
			BubbleID:  bubbleID,
			Type:      bubbleType,
			Grouping:  &BubbleGrouping{IsRenderable: true, HasText: turn.Text != ""},
			CreatedAt: createdAt,
		}
	}

	// Build a complete composerData JSON that matches Cursor's expected schema.
	// Cursor filters sessions based on fields like hasLoaded, isDraft, status, and isAgentic;
	// omitting them causes the session to be invisible in the UI even if the data is present.

	composerMap := map[string]interface{}{
		// Identity. _v pins the composer schema version this record claims (17, as
		// observed in sessions written by Cursor 3.12). If a future Cursor bumps its
		// schema it will either migrate this record on load or silently stop showing
		// it — in the latter case this literal needs re-syncing against a current
		// database.
		"_v":         17,
		"composerId": newID,
		"name":       spi.ResumedSessionTitle(data.Slug),
		// Visibility-critical fields: Cursor hides sessions where these are absent or wrong.
		"hasLoaded":   true,
		"isDraft":     false,
		"status":      "completed",
		"isAgentic":   true,
		"unifiedMode": "agent", // string at composer level (int on bubbles)
		// Timestamps
		"createdAt":     nowMs,
		"lastUpdatedAt": nowMs + int64(len(turns))*1000,
		// workspaceIdentifier associates this session with its workspace so Cursor's Agent
		// sidebar shows it under the right project. Without this field Cursor ignores the session.
		"workspaceIdentifier": map[string]interface{}{
			"id":  workspace.ID,
			"uri": vscode.WorkspaceURIMap(workspaceRoot),
		},
		// Conversation index
		"fullConversationHeadersOnly": headers,
		// Standard empty fields that Cursor expects to be present.
		"richText":                      `{"root":{"children":[{"children":[],"format":"","indent":0,"type":"paragraph","version":1}],"format":"","indent":0,"type":"root","version":1}}`,
		"text":                          "",
		"conversationMap":               map[string]interface{}{},
		"generatingBubbleIds":           []interface{}{},
		"isReadingLongFile":             false,
		"codeBlockData":                 map[string]interface{}{},
		"originalFileStates":            map[string]interface{}{},
		"newlyCreatedFiles":             []interface{}{},
		"newlyCreatedFolders":           []interface{}{},
		"hasChangedContext":             false,
		"activeTabsShouldBeReactive":    false,
		"capabilities":                  []interface{}{},
		"context":                       map[string]interface{}{},
		"isFileListExpanded":            false,
		"canvasPillCollapsed":           false,
		"browserChipManuallyDisabled":   false,
		"browserChipManuallyEnabled":    false,
		"forceMode":                     "edit",
		"usageData":                     map[string]interface{}{},
		"contextUsagePercent":           0,
		"allAttachedFileCodeChunksUris": []interface{}{},
		"modelConfig":                   map[string]interface{}{"modelName": "default", "maxMode": false, "selectedModels": []interface{}{}},
		"subComposerIds":                []interface{}{},
		"subagentComposerIds":           []interface{}{},
		"capabilityContexts":            []interface{}{},
		"todos":                         []interface{}{},
		"isQueueExpanded":               true,
		"hasUnreadMessages":             false,
		"gitHubPromptDismissed":         false,
		"totalLinesAdded":               0,
		"totalLinesRemoved":             0,
		"addedFiles":                    0,
		"removedFiles":                  0,
		"filesChangedCount":             0,
		"subtitle":                      "",
		"isCreatingWorktree":            false,
		"isApplyingWorktree":            false,
		"isUndoingWorktree":             false,
		"applied":                       false,
		"pendingCreateWorktree":         false,
		"worktreeStartedReadOnly":       false,
		"isBestOfNSubcomposer":          false,
		"isBestOfNParent":               false,
		"isSpec":                        false,
		"isProject":                     false,
		"isSpecSubagentDone":            false,
		"isContinuationInProgress":      false,
		"stopHookLoopCount":             0,
		"trackedGitRepos":               []interface{}{},
		// isNAL and agentBackend mirror what Cursor 3 writes for its own new agent
		// sessions (values observed in real state.vscdb records); Cursor's loader
		// expects them on agent-mode composers.
		"isNAL":                   true,
		"agentBackend":            "cursor-agent",
		"planModeSuggestionUsed":  false,
		"debugModeSuggestionUsed": false,
		"queueItems":              []interface{}{},
	}
	composerJSON, err := json.Marshal(composerMap)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal composer data: %w", err)
	}

	db, err := OpenDatabaseReadWrite(globalDbPath)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to open Cursor IDE database for writing: %w", err)
	}
	defer func() {
		if closeErr := db.Close(); closeErr != nil {
			slog.Warn("Failed to close Cursor IDE database after reconstruction", "error", closeErr)
		}
	}()

	if err := InsertComposerSession(db, newID, composerJSON, bubbles); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to write reconstructed session to Cursor IDE database: %w", err)
	}

	slog.Info("Reconstructed session written to Cursor IDE global database",
		"composerID", newID, "turns", len(turns), "dbPath", globalDbPath)

	regMeta := ComposerHeadMeta{
		ComposerID:    newID,
		Name:          spi.ResumedSessionTitle(data.Slug),
		CreatedAt:     nowMs,
		LastUpdatedAt: nowMs + int64(len(turns))*1000,
		WorkspaceID:   workspace.ID,
	}
	// Write to the global composer.composerHeaders (ItemTable) — the sidebar source for
	// Cursor versions before 3.12 (newer versions use the glass keys registered below).
	if hdrErr := WriteGlobalComposerHeader(globalDbPath, regMeta, workspaceRoot); hdrErr != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to write global composer header: %w", hdrErr)
	}
	// Register in the glass sidebar keys — what Cursor >= 3.12 actually builds its
	// Agent sidebar from. Without this the session exists but is never listed.
	if glassErr := RegisterGlassProjectMembership(globalDbPath, newID, workspace.ID, workspaceRoot); glassErr != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to register session in Cursor sidebar: %w", glassErr)
	}
	// Append to selectedComposerIds so Cursor opens the resumed session as an active tab.
	// This is a UX convenience only — sidebar visibility comes from composer.composerHeaders above.
	if selErr := AppendToSelectedComposerIDs(workspace.StateDBPath(), newID); selErr != nil {
		slog.Warn("Failed to register session as active tab in workspace", "composerID", newID, "error", selErr)
	}
	slog.Info("Reconstructed session registered in Cursor IDE",
		"composerID", newID, "workspaceID", workspace.ID)

	// The resume flow writes rec.Content to the path returned by NativeSessionPath.
	// Cursor IDE uses a shared global DB rather than per-session files, so we return
	// empty content; NativeSessionPath points to a harmless temp path.
	return &spi.ReconstructedSession{
		SessionID: newID,
		Filename:  newID,
		Content:   []byte{},
	}, nil
}

// NativeSessionPath returns a temp path where the resume flow writes the (empty) sentinel
// content. Cursor IDE sessions live in the shared global state.vscdb, not per-session
// files, so the actual data was already written in ReconstructSession. The temp file is
// harmless and will be cleaned up by the OS.
func (p *Provider) NativeSessionPath(_ string, filename string) (string, error) {
package spi

import (
	"database/sql"
	"fmt"
	"log/slog"
	"strings"

	_ "modernc.org/sqlite" // Pure Go SQLite driver
)

// BusyTimeoutPragma is appended to SQLite DSNs so each new connection waits for a
// briefly-held lock instead of failing immediately with SQLITE_BUSY. The agent that
// owns the database may be running and writing to it (e.g. during a checkpoint), so
// without a busy timeout a read or a journal-mode change can fail on a transient lock.
const BusyTimeoutPragma = "_pragma=busy_timeout(5000)"

// EnsureWALMode ensures the database is running in WAL journal mode. WAL lets our
// read-only connections and the owning agent's writer proceed concurrently without
// blocking each other, and guarantees the -wal file exists for watchers that rely
// on fsnotify events. This must open a read-write connection because PRAGMA
// journal_mode cannot change the mode on a read-only connection. It is intended to
// be called once per database, not on every read.
func EnsureWALMode(dbPath string) error {
	// Open read-write to be able to change journal mode. mode=rw (not the
	// default create-if-missing) so a wrong path errors instead of leaving a
	// stray empty database behind; the file: scheme is required because the
	// driver only honors mode= on URI-form DSNs.
	db, err := sql.Open("sqlite", "file:"+dbPath+"?mode=rw&"+BusyTimeoutPragma)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to open database for WAL check: %w", err)
	}
	defer func() {
		if closeErr := db.Close(); closeErr != nil {
			slog.Warn("Failed to close database after WAL check", "error", closeErr)
		}
	}()

	// Check current journal mode
	var currentMode string
	if err := db.QueryRow("PRAGMA journal_mode").Scan(&currentMode); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to query journal mode: %w", err)
	}

	if strings.EqualFold(currentMode, "wal") {
		slog.Debug("Database already in WAL mode", "path", dbPath)
		return nil
	}

	// Switch to WAL mode. QueryRow rather than Exec because the pragma returns
	// the resulting mode as a row; checking it catches a silent failure to switch.
	var newMode string
	if err := db.QueryRow("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL").Scan(&newMode); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to set WAL mode: %w", err)
	}

	if !strings.EqualFold(newMode, "wal") {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to enable WAL mode: got %q instead", newMode)
	}

	slog.Info("Enabled WAL mode on database", "path", dbPath)
	return nil
}
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-09-22 22:58:32Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="shell" data-tool-name="Bash"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Bash**</summary>
Summarize OpenCode message schemas from OpenAPI

```bash
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
d=json.load(open("/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sean-Source-SpecStory-getspecstory-specstory-cli/38a72af2-5eab-4124-a484-d558ff7aff6c/scratchpad/openapi.json"))
S=d["components"]["schemas"]
def short(o,depth=0):
    if isinstance(o,dict):
        if "$ref" in o: return o["$ref"].split("/")[-1]
        if "properties" in o:
            req=set(o.get("required",[]))
            return {k+("" if k in req else "?"):short(v,depth+1) for k,v in o["properties"].items()}
        for key in ("anyOf","oneOf","allOf"):
            if key in o: return {key:[short(x,depth+1) for x in o[key]]}
        if o.get("type")=="array": return [short(o.get("items",{}),depth+1)]
        if "enum" in o: return "enum"+json.dumps(o["enum"])
        if "const" in o: return "const:"+json.dumps(o["const"])
        return o.get("type","?")
    return o
for k in sorted(S):
    if k.startswith("Session.Message") or k.startswith("Tool.") or k in("Session.Info","Session",):
        print("##",k); print(json.dumps(short(S[k]),indent=None)[:1500])
EOF
```

```text
     hello.py lines 5–6 now define farewell(), and the new farewell.py defines an identical function. This is the kind of duplication that drifts: if
```

```bash
import json,sys
def clip(o):
  if isinstance(o,str): return o if len(o)<300 else o[:300]+"…<%d>"%len(o)
  if isinstance(o,dict): return {k:clip(v) for k,v in o.items() if k!="reasoningEncryptedContent"}
  if isinstance(o,list): return [clip(x) for x in o]
  return o
for r in json.load(sys.stdin):
  d=json.loads(r["data"])
  if r["type"]=="assistant":
    d["content"]=[{"type":c["type"],**({"name":c["name"]} if c["type"]=="tool" else {"text":clip(c.get("text",""))})} for c in d["content"]]
  print(r["seq"],r["type"],json.dumps(clip(d))[:900])'
```

```text
// materializeReconstructed reconstructs data into plan.to's native store under cwd, durably writes

func materializeReconstructed(plan *resumePlan, cwd string, data *schema.SessionData, note string) (*spi.ReconstructedSession, error) {
	rec, err := plan.to.ReconstructSession(data, spi.ReconstructOptions{
```

```text
39	func (p *Provider) Check(customCommand string) spi.CheckResult {
40		cmdName, _ := parseMuseCommand(customCommand)
41		isCustom := customCommand != ""
42		attempt := analytics.CheckAttempt{
43			Provider:      "muse",
44			CustomCommand: isCustom,
45			CommandPath:   cmdName,
46			VersionFlag:   versionFlag,
47		}
48	
49		slog.Info("Check: verifying Muse Code installation", "command", cmdName, "customCommand", isCustom)
50	
51		resolvedPath, err := spi.LookPathForCheck(cmdName)
52		if err != nil {
53			errorType := spi.ClassifyCheckError(err)
54			slog.Info("Check: binary lookup failed", "command", cmdName, "error", err)
55			errorMessage := buildMuseCheckErrorMessage(errorType, cmdName, isCustom, "")
56			analytics.TrackCheckFailure(attempt, errorType, err.Error(), "")
57			return spi.CheckResult{
58				Success:      false,
59				ErrorType:    errorType,
60				Location:     "",
61				ErrorMessage: errorMessage,
62			}
63		}
64		attempt.ResolvedPath = resolvedPath
65	
66		cmd := exec.Command(resolvedPath, versionFlag)
67		var stdout bytes.Buffer
68		var stderr bytes.Buffer
69		cmd.Stdout = &stdout
70		cmd.Stderr = &stderr
71	
72		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
73			errorType := spi.ClassifyCheckExecutionError(err)
74			stderrOutput := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
75			slog.Info("Check: version probe failed",
76				"resolved", resolvedPath,
77				"errorType", errorType,
78				"error", err,
79				"stderr", stderrOutput)
80			errorMessage := buildMuseCheckErrorMessage(errorType, resolvedPath, isCustom, stderrOutput)
81			analytics.TrackCheckFailure(attempt, errorType, err.Error(), stderrOutput)
82	
83			return spi.CheckResult{
84				Success:      false,
85				ErrorType:    errorType,
86				Location:     resolvedPath,
87				ErrorMessage: errorMessage,
88			}
89		}
90	
91		// A binary that runs but prints nothing still passes the check; report a
92		// placeholder rather than an empty version so the result reads unambiguously.
93		version := strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
94		if version == "" {
95			version = "unknown"
96		}
97		slog.Info("Check: succeeded", "resolved", resolvedPath, "version", version)
98		analytics.TrackCheckSuccess(attempt, version)
99	
100		return spi.CheckResult{
101			Success:  true,
102			Version:  version,
103			Location: resolvedPath,
104		}
105	}

107	func buildMuseCheckErrorMessage(errorType string, museCmd string, isCustom bool, stderr string) string {
108		var b strings.Builder
109	
110		switch errorType {
111		case spi.CheckErrorNotFound:
112			b.WriteString("Muse Code could not be found.\n\n")
113			if isCustom {
114				b.WriteString("• Verify the path you supplied actually points to the `muse` executable.\n")
115				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "• Provided command: %s\n", museCmd)
116			} else {
117				b.WriteString("• Install Muse Code and ensure `muse` is on your PATH.\n")
118				b.WriteString("• Or pass a custom command via `specstory check muse -c \"path/to/muse\"`.\n")
119			}
120		case spi.CheckErrorPermissionDenied:
121			b.WriteString("Muse Code exists but isn't executable.\n\n")
122			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "• Fix permissions: `chmod +x %s`\n", museCmd)
123			b.WriteString("• Some package managers install the binary as root; run SpecStory with a path you can execute.\n")
124		default:
125			b.WriteString("`muse --version` failed.\n\n")
126			if stderr != "" {
127				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Error output:\n%s\n\n", stderr)
128			}
129			b.WriteString("• Try running `muse --version` directly in your terminal.\n")
130			b.WriteString("• If you upgraded recently, reinstall the CLI to refresh dependencies.\n")
131		}
132	
133		return b.String()
134	}

155			sessionsRoot, rootErr := GetMuseSessionsDir()
156			if rootErr != nil || sessionsRoot == "" {
157				fmt.Println("No Muse Code sessions found.")
158				fmt.Println("Start a Muse Code session in this project (e.g. `muse`) so a transcript is created.")
159				return false
160			}
161			if _, statErr := os.Stat(sessionsRoot); statErr != nil {
162				fmt.Printf("Muse Code sessions directory not found (%s).\n", sessionsRoot)
163				fmt.Println("Run Muse Code once (e.g. `muse`) so the session store is created, then rerun this command.")
164				return false
165			}
166			fmt.Printf("Muse Code sessions exist under %s but none record this project as their workspace root.\n", sessionsRoot)
167			fmt.Println("Start a Muse Code session from this directory so the provider can pick it up.")
168		}
169		return false
170	}
171	
172	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessions(projectPath string, debugRaw bool, progress spi.ProgressCallback) ([]spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
173		projectPath, err := defaultProjectPath(projectPath)
174		if err != nil {
175			return nil, err
176		}
177	
178		files, err := findMuseSessions(projectPath)
179		if err != nil {
180			return nil, err
181		}
182	
183		var result []spi.AgentChatSession
184		for i, file := range files {
185			if chatSession := parseAndConvert(file.Path, projectPath, debugRaw); chatSession != nil {
186				result = append(result, *chatSession)
187			}
188	
189			// Report progress after each session
190			if progress != nil {
191				progress(i+1, len(files))
192			}
193		}
194		return result, nil
195	}
196	
197	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSession(projectPath string, sessionID string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
198		projectPath, err := defaultProjectPath(projectPath)
199		if err != nil {
200			return nil, err
201		}
202	
203		// The store is keyed by session id (the id IS the directory name), so a
204		// glob resolves the path without reading any transcript.
205		//
206		// The id alone does not establish ownership, though: the store is global, so
207		// the glob will just as happily find another project's session. Confirm the
208		// transcript names this project before converting it — conversion stamps the
209		// requested project onto the result, so returning an unchecked match would
210		// file one project's conversation under another. The scan below applies the
211		// same rule via findMuseSessions.
212		directPath, err := findMuseSessionPathByID(sessionID)
213		if err != nil {
214			return nil, err
215		}
216		if directPath != "" && sessionFileBelongsToProject(directPath, projectPath) {
217			if chatSession := parseAndConvert(directPath, projectPath, debugRaw); chatSession != nil {
218				return chatSession, nil
219			}
220		}
221	
222		// Fall back to a scan: the id may name a session recorded under a layout
223		// the glob does not cover.
224		files, err := findMuseSessions(projectPath)
225		if err != nil {
226			return nil, err
227		}
228		for _, file := range files {
229			if file.SessionID == sessionID {
230				return parseAndConvert(file.Path, projectPath, debugRaw), nil
231			}
232		}
233	
234		return nil, nil
235	}
236	
237	// GetAgentChatSessionByPath parses a single session directly from its known
238	// native file path, skipping by-id discovery. Used by reindex (which already
239	// holds NativePath from enumeration) to keep resolving N sessions O(N).
240	func (p *Provider) GetAgentChatSessionByPath(nativePath string, originCwd string, debugRaw bool) (*spi.AgentChatSession, error) {
241		session, err := ParseSessionFile(nativePath)
242		if err != nil {
243			return nil, err
244		}
245		if len(session.Events) == 0 {
246			return nil, nil
247		}
248		return convertToAgentChatSession(session, originCwd, debugRaw), nil
249	}
250	
251	// parseAndConvert parses one transcript and converts it, logging and returning
252	// nil for files that are unreadable or hold no conversation yet.
253	func parseAndConvert(filePath string, workspaceRoot string, debugRaw bool) *spi.AgentChatSession {
254		session, err := ParseSessionFile(filePath)
255		if err != nil {
256			slog.Warn("parseAndConvert: Failed to parse Muse session file, skipping",
257				"file", filePath, "error", err)
258			return nil
259		}
260		if len(session.Events) == 0 {
261			slog.Debug("parseAndConvert: Session file has no conversation events", "file", filePath)
262			return nil
263		}
264		return convertToAgentChatSession(session, workspaceRoot, debugRaw)
265	}
266	
267	// convertToAgentChatSession converts a MuseSession to the provider-agnostic
268	// AgentChatSession format. Used by both sync mode and watch mode.
269	func convertToAgentChatSession(session *MuseSession, workspaceRoot string, debugRaw bool) *spi.AgentChatSession {
270		sessionData, err := GenerateAgentSession(session, workspaceRoot)
271		if err != nil {
272			slog.Error("convertToAgentChatSession: failed to generate session data",
273				"sessionId", session.ID,
274				"error", err)
275			return nil
276		}
277	
278		slug := museSessionSlug(session)
279		sessionData.Slug = slug
280	
281		// Use the parsing snapshot: a live transcript can grow before conversion.
282		var rawData strings.Builder
283		for _, record := range session.RawRecords {
284			rawData.Write(record)
285		}
286	
287		if debugRaw {
288			if err := writeDebugRawFiles(session); err != nil {
289				slog.Warn("convertToAgentChatSession: failed to write debug files",
290					"sessionId", session.ID,
291					"path", spi.GetDebugDir(session.ID),
292					"error", err)
293			}
294		}
295	
296		return &spi.AgentChatSession{
297			SessionID:   session.ID,
298			CreatedAt:   session.StartTime,
299			Slug:        slug,
300			SessionData: sessionData,
301			RawData:     rawData.String(),
302		}
303	}
304	
305	// museSessionSlug derives the filename-safe slug from the prompt that opened
306	// the session.
307	func museSessionSlug(session *MuseSession) string {
308		if prompt := session.FirstUserPrompt(); prompt != "" {
309			if slug := spi.GenerateFilenameFromUserMessage(prompt); slug != "" {
310				return slug
311			}
312		}
313		return "muse-session"
314	}
315	
316	// writeDebugRawFiles preserves native envelopes in source order, including
317	// metadata, telemetry, and task streams omitted from the rendered conversation.
318	func writeDebugRawFiles(session *MuseSession) error {
319		return spi.WriteDebugRecords(spi.GetDebugDir(session.ID), session.RawRecords)
320	}
321	
322	// ListAgentChatSessions retrieves lightweight session metadata without full
323	// conversion.
324	//
325	// Each matching transcript is read twice: findMuseSessions filters the global
326	// store by a bounded header scan, and only this project's matches pay for the
327	// full parse here — the first prompt and timestamps the metadata needs live in
328	// the event log, not the header, so the second read cannot be avoided without
329	// giving up the cheap cross-project filter.
330	func (p *Provider) ListAgentChatSessions(projectPath string) ([]spi.SessionMetadata, error) {
331		projectPath, err := defaultProjectPath(projectPath)
332		if err != nil {
333			return nil, err
334		}
335	
336		files, err := findMuseSessions(projectPath)
337		if err != nil {
338			return nil, err
339		}
340	
341		result := make([]spi.SessionMetadata, 0, len(files))
342		for _, file := range files {
343			session, err := ParseSessionFile(file.Path)
344			if err != nil {
345				slog.Warn("ListAgentChatSessions: Failed to parse session file, skipping",
346					"file", file.Path, "error", err)
347				continue
348			}
349			metadata := extractMuseSessionMetadata(session)
350			if metadata == nil {
351				slog.Debug("ListAgentChatSessions: Skipping session with no user prompt", "sessionID", session.ID)
352				continue
353			}
354			result = append(result, *metadata)
355		}
356	
357		return result, nil
358	}
359	
360	// extractMuseSessionMetadata extracts lightweight metadata from a Muse session.
361	// Returns nil if the session never received a user prompt (a session that
362	// crashed during startup, or a transcript holding only telemetry).
363	func extractMuseSessionMetadata(session *MuseSession) *spi.SessionMetadata {
364		firstPrompt := session.FirstUserPrompt()
365		if firstPrompt == "" {
366			return nil
367		}
368	
369		return &spi.SessionMetadata{
370			SessionID: session.ID,
371			CreatedAt: session.StartTime,
372			Slug:      museSessionSlug(session),
373			Name:      spi.GenerateReadableName(firstPrompt),
374		}
375	}
376	
377	// ListAllAgentChatSessions enumerates every session in this provider's native
378	// store, regardless of project. See docs/SESSIONS-DB.md.
379	//
380	// Muse's store is global and date-sharded, so the project association comes
381	// from the workspace_root recorded inside each transcript rather than from the
382	// path.
383	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessions() ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
384		return p.ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(nil)
385	}
386	
387	// ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress enumerates all sessions while reporting
388	// scan progress into r (nil-safe). Used by `specstory reindex`.
389	func (p *Provider) ListAllAgentChatSessionsProgress(r *spi.ScanReporter) ([]spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
390		sessionsRoot, err := GetMuseSessionsDir()
391		if err != nil {
392			return nil, err
393		}
394		if _, err := os.Stat(sessionsRoot); err != nil {
395			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
396				return []spi.GlobalSessionRef{}, nil
397			}
398			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read Muse sessions directory: %w", err)
399		}
400	
401		return spi.ScanSessionsInParallel(sessionsRoot, "muse", r, func(path string) (*spi.GlobalSessionRef, error) {
402			// Only top-level <session-id>/session.jsonl files are sessions;
403			// subagent transcripts belong to their parent.
404			if filepath.Base(path) != sessionFileName || IsSubagentTranscript(path) {
405				return nil, nil
406			}
407	
408			session, err := ParseSessionFile(path)
409			if err != nil {
410				return nil, err
411			}
412			metadata := extractMuseSessionMetadata(session)
413			if metadata == nil {
414				return nil, nil // telemetry-only or prompt-less session
415			}
416	
417			return &spi.GlobalSessionRef{
418				SessionID:  metadata.SessionID,
419				CreatedAt:  metadata.CreatedAt,
420				Slug:       metadata.Slug,
421				Name:       metadata.Name,
422				NativePath: path,
423				OriginCwd:  session.WorkspaceRoot,
424			}, nil
425		})
426	}
427	
428	func (p *Provider) ExecAgentAndWatch(projectPath string, customCommand string, resumeSessionID string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
429		slog.Info("ExecAgentAndWatch: Starting Muse Code", "project", projectPath)
430	
431		SetWatcherDebugRaw(debugRaw)
432		if err := WatchMuseProject(projectPath, sessionCallback); err != nil {
433			slog.Error("Failed to start watcher", "error", err)
434		}
435		defer StopWatcher()
436	
437		if resumeSessionID != "" {
438			slog.Info("Attempting to resume Muse Code session", "sessionId", resumeSessionID)
439		}
440	
441		return ExecuteMuse(customCommand, resumeSessionID)
442	}
443	
444	// WatchAgent watches for Muse Code agent activity and calls the callback with
445	// an AgentChatSession. Does NOT execute the agent - only watches for activity.
446	// Runs until error or context cancellation (blocks indefinitely).
447	func (p *Provider) WatchAgent(ctx context.Context, projectPath string, debugRaw bool, sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession)) error {
448		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Starting Muse Code activity monitoring",
449			"projectPath", projectPath,
450			"debugRaw", debugRaw)
451	
452		SetWatcherDebugRaw(debugRaw)
453	
454		if err := WatchMuseProject(projectPath, sessionCallback); err != nil {
455			slog.Error("WatchAgent: Failed to start Muse session watcher", "error", err)
456			return fmt.Errorf("failed to start watcher: %w", err)
457		}
458	
459		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Watcher started, blocking until context cancelled")
460		<-ctx.Done()
461	
462		slog.Info("WatchAgent: Context cancelled, stopping watcher")
463		StopWatcher()
464	
465		return ctx.Err()
466	}
```

```text
1	package musecode
2	
3	import (
4		"errors"
5		"fmt"
6		"log/slog"
7		"os"
8		"os/exec"
9	
10		"github.com/specstoryai/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/spi"
11	)
12	
13	// resumeSubcommand is how Muse Code continues a session: `muse resume <id>`,
14	// a subcommand rather than a flag (like Codex, unlike Qwen's --resume).
15	const resumeSubcommand = "resume"
16	
17	// defaultMuseCommand is used when no custom command is configured. No PATH
18	// probing here: Check reports a missing binary with remediation steps, and
19	// exec surfaces the OS error directly, so a lookup would only duplicate both.
20	const defaultMuseCommand = "muse"
21	
22	// parseMuseCommand parses a custom command string into executable and arguments.
23	func parseMuseCommand(customCommand string) (string, []string) {
24		if customCommand != "" {
25			parts := spi.SplitCommandLine(customCommand)
26			if len(parts) > 0 {
27				return parts[0], parts[1:]
28			}
29		}
30		return defaultMuseCommand, nil
31	}
32	
33	// ExecuteMuse runs the Muse Code CLI, optionally resuming an existing session.
34	// Return the agent's exit status so ExecAgentAndWatch can stop the watcher and
35	// join in-flight saves before the CLI applies that status to the process.
36	func ExecuteMuse(customCommand string, resumeSessionID string) error {
37		museCmd, args := parseMuseCommand(customCommand)
38	
39		args = spi.EnsureResumeArgs(args, resumeSubcommand, resumeSessionID)
40		if resumeSessionID != "" {
41			slog.Info("ExecuteMuse: Resuming Muse Code session", "sessionId", resumeSessionID, "args", args)
42		}
43	
44		cmd := exec.Command(museCmd, args...)
45	
46		// Interactive mode: connect to the user's terminal
47		cmd.Stdin = os.Stdin
48		cmd.Stdout = os.Stdout
49		cmd.Stderr = os.Stderr
50	
51		slog.Info("ExecuteMuse: Starting Muse Code process", "command", museCmd, "args", args)
52		if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
53			return fmt.Errorf("failed to start muse: %w", err)
54		}
55	
56		slog.Info("ExecuteMuse: Waiting for Muse Code to exit")
57		if err := cmd.Wait(); err != nil {
58			var exitErr *exec.ExitError
59			if errors.As(err, &exitErr) {
60				exitCode := exitErr.ExitCode()
61				slog.Info("ExecuteMuse: Muse Code exited", "exitCode", exitCode)
62				return &spi.AgentExitError{Agent: "Muse Code", Code: exitCode}
63			}
64			return fmt.Errorf("muse execution failed: %w", err)
65		}
66	
67		slog.Info("ExecuteMuse: Muse Code exited normally", "exitCode", 0)
68		return nil
69	}
70
```

```text
67	// NewCursorIDEWatcher creates a new watcher for Cursor IDE databases
68	func NewCursorIDEWatcher(

70		debugRaw bool,
71		sessionCallback func(*spi.AgentChatSession),
72		checkInterval time.Duration,
73	) (*CursorIDEWatcher, error) {
74		// A nil callback would only surface as a panic deep inside checkForChanges,
75		// long after construction — fail fast here instead.
76		if sessionCallback == nil {
77			return nil, fmt.Errorf("sessionCallback must not be nil")
78		}
79	
80		// Find all workspaces matching the project (a project can match more than one
81		// workspace entry — e.g. opened via .code-workspace, over SSH, or from WSL).
82		workspaces, err := FindAllWorkspacesForProject(projectPath)
83		if err != nil {
84			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to find workspace for project: %w", err)
85		}

91		}

94		fsWatcher, err := fsnotify.NewWatcher()
95		if err != nil {
96			return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create file watcher: %w", err)
97		}
98	
99		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
100	
101		// Set default check interval if not provided
102		if checkInterval == 0 {
103			checkInterval = defaultCheckInterval
104		}
105	
106		return &CursorIDEWatcher{
107			projectPath:      projectPath,
108			workspaces:       workspaces,
109			globalDbPath:     globalDbPath,

111			sessionCallback:  sessionCallback,

115			checkInterval:    checkInterval,
116			throttleDuration: 10 * time.Second,
117			// Zero value, not time.Now(): lastThrottledCall means "the last time a check
118			// actually ran," not "when the watcher was constructed." Seeding it with the
119			// current time made the very first real check (5s after Start()) look like it

130	// Start begins monitoring the Cursor IDE databases
131	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) Start() error {
132		slog.Info("Starting Cursor IDE watcher",
133			"projectPath", w.projectPath,
134			"workspaceCount", len(w.workspaces),
135			"globalDbPath", w.globalDbPath,
136			"checkInterval", w.checkInterval,
137			"throttleDuration", w.throttleDuration)

139		// Ensure WAL mode is enabled on all databases before watching.
140		// WAL mode is required so that the -wal file exists for fsnotify to detect changes.
141		// This is a one-time read-write operation at startup; all subsequent reads are read-only.
142		for _, ws := range w.workspaces {
143			if err := spi.EnsureWALMode(ws.StateDBPath()); err != nil {
144				slog.Warn("Failed to ensure WAL mode on workspace database",
145					"workspaceID", ws.ID,
146					"error", err)
147			}
148		}
149		if err := spi.EnsureWALMode(w.globalDbPath); err != nil {
150			slog.Warn("Failed to ensure WAL mode on global database", "error", err)
151		}
152	
153		// Seed knownComposers with the sessions that already exist so startup doesn't
154		// re-emit every historical session — matching the other providers' watchers
155		// (e.g. Cursor CLI's SetInitialState). Sessions updated after this point still
156		// process because their lastUpdatedAt advances past the seeded watermark.
157		w.seedKnownComposers()

160		for _, ws := range w.workspaces {

192	// the worst case is that the first check re-emits existing sessions, which is the exact
193	// behavior this seeding exists to avoid, not a correctness problem.
194	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) seedKnownComposers() {
195		// One lightweight scan serves both needs here: discovery (via projectComposerIDs)
196		// and the per-composer timestamps read below.
197		composers, err := LoadAllComposerDataLightweight(w.globalDbPath)
198		if err != nil {
199			slog.Warn("Failed to seed existing sessions; first check may re-emit them", "error", err)
200			return
201		}
202		composerIDs, err := projectComposerIDs(composers, w.projectPath, w.workspaces)
203		if err != nil || len(composerIDs) == 0 {
204			return
205		}
206	
207		w.mu.Lock()
208		defer w.mu.Unlock()
209		seeded := 0
210		for _, composerID := range composerIDs {
211			composer, exists := composers[composerID]
212			if !exists {
213				continue
214			}
215			timestamp := composer.LastUpdatedAt
216			if timestamp == 0 {
217				timestamp = composer.CreatedAt
218			}
219			w.knownComposers[composerID] = timestamp
220			seeded++
221		}
222		slog.Debug("Seeded existing sessions as known", "count", seeded)
223	}
224	
225	// Stop gracefully stops the watcher
226	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) Stop() {
227		slog.Info("Stopping Cursor IDE watcher")
228	
229		// Stop the initial-check timer in case it hasn't fired yet — no point starting a
230		// check that would just have to be waited on below.
231		if w.initialCheckTimer != nil {
232			w.initialCheckTimer.Stop()
233		}
234	
235		// Perform one final check before stopping
236		slog.Info("Performing final check for changes before stopping")
237		w.checkForChanges("shutdown")
238	
239		// Close fsnotify watcher
240		if w.fsWatcher != nil {
241			if err := w.fsWatcher.Close(); err != nil {
242				slog.Warn("Error closing fsnotify watcher", "error", err)
243			}
244		}
245	
246		// Cancel under w.mu, then wait. Every check-spawning wg.Add happens under this
247		// lock (triggerCheck/executePendingCheck), so once cancel lands no trigger can
248		// pass the ctx check and Add after Wait has started — Add-concurrent-with-Wait
249		// on a drained WaitGroup is a documented misuse.
250		w.mu.Lock()
251		w.cancel()
252		w.mu.Unlock()
253		w.wg.Wait()
254	
255		// Wait for any pending callback goroutines to complete
256		slog.Info("Waiting for pending callbacks to complete")
257		w.callbackWg.Wait()
258	
259		slog.Info("Cursor IDE watcher stopped")
260	}
261	
262	// watchDatabaseFiles sets up file watching for a database and its WAL file.
263	//
264	// Why the parent directory instead of the files themselves: in WAL mode nearly every
265	// write lands in state.vscdb-wal, and SQLite deletes that file when the last
266	// connection closes and recreates it on the next open. A watch on the file itself is
267	// never added when the file doesn't exist yet (watcher started before Cursor), and
268	// dies with the inode when Cursor checkpoints/restarts — silently degrading all
269	// updates to the 2-minute safety-net poll. A directory watch keeps delivering
270	// Create/Write events for the db and its -wal across those lifecycles.
271	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) watchDatabaseFiles(dbPath string) error {
272		dir := filepath.Dir(dbPath)
273		if err := w.fsWatcher.Add(dir); err != nil {
274			// Log but don't fail - we'll rely on polling
275			slog.Warn("Failed to watch database directory", "dir", dir, "error", err)
276			return err
277		}
278	
279		// Register the db path so handleFileEvents can filter directory events
280		// down to this database's files.
281		w.watchedDBPaths = append(w.watchedDBPaths, dbPath)
282		slog.Debug("Watching database directory", "dir", dir, "dbPath", dbPath)
283	
284		return nil
285	}
286	
287	// isWatchedDBFile reports whether a file event path belongs to one of the watched
288	// databases (the db file itself or a sibling like -wal/-shm/-journal).
289	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) isWatchedDBFile(name string) bool {
290		for _, dbPath := range w.watchedDBPaths {
291			if name == dbPath || strings.HasPrefix(name, dbPath+"-") {
292				return true
293			}
294		}
295		return false
296	}
297	
298	// handleFileEvents processes file system events from fsnotify
299	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) handleFileEvents() {
300		for {
301			select {
302			case <-w.ctx.Done():
303				return
304	
305			case event, ok := <-w.fsWatcher.Events:
306				if !ok {
307					return
308				}
309	
310				// Only care about Write and Create events on the database files —
311				// the watch is on the parent directory, so unrelated neighbors
312				// (e.g. workspace.json) must be filtered out.
313				if (event.Has(fsnotify.Write) || event.Has(fsnotify.Create)) && w.isWatchedDBFile(event.Name) {
314					slog.Debug("Database file changed", "path", event.Name, "op", event.Op)
315					w.triggerCheck("file-change")
316				}
317	
318			case err, ok := <-w.fsWatcher.Errors:
319				if !ok {
320					return
321				}
322				slog.Warn("File watcher error", "error", err)
323			}
324		}
325	}
326	
327	// safetyNetPoller ensures we check the database periodically even if file events are missed
328	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) safetyNetPoller() {
329		ticker := time.NewTicker(w.checkInterval)
330		defer ticker.Stop()
331	
332		for {
333			select {
334			case <-w.ctx.Done():
335				return
336			case <-ticker.C:
337				slog.Debug("Safety net poll triggered")
338				w.triggerCheck("poll")
339			}
340		}
341	}
342	
343	// triggerCheck requests a check, respecting throttle limits
344	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) triggerCheck(trigger string) {
345		w.mu.Lock()
346		defer w.mu.Unlock()
347	
348		// Shutdown guard: Stop() cancels the context under this same lock, so a trigger
349		// arriving after cancellation must not wg.Add (Stop may already be in wg.Wait).
350		// This covers the throttle branch below; runCheckAsync re-checks for its own path.
351		if w.ctx.Err() != nil {
352			return
353		}
354	
355		now := time.Now()
356		timeSinceLastCall := now.Sub(w.lastThrottledCall)
357	
358		if timeSinceLastCall < w.throttleDuration {
359			// Within throttle window - mark as pending
360			if !w.pendingCheck {
361				w.pendingCheck = true
362				// Schedule a check after throttle duration expires
363				delay := w.throttleDuration - timeSinceLastCall
364				slog.Debug("Check throttled, will retry after delay",
365					"trigger", trigger,
366					"delay", delay)
367	
368				w.wg.Go(func() {
369					timer := time.NewTimer(delay)
370					defer timer.Stop()
371					select {
372					case <-w.ctx.Done():
373						return
374					case <-timer.C:
375						w.executePendingCheck()
376					}
377				})
378			}
379			return
380		}
381	
382		// Execute immediately
383		w.lastThrottledCall = now
384		w.pendingCheck = false
385		w.runCheckAsync(trigger)
386	}
387	
388	// runCheckAsync runs checkForChanges in a new goroutine tracked by w.wg, so Stop()'s
389	// w.wg.Wait() actually waits for it instead of returning while it's still running.
390	// It's a no-op if the watcher's context is already cancelled.
391	// Must be called with w.mu held: Stop() cancels the context under the same lock, which
392	// is what makes the ctx check and the wg registration here atomic with respect to shutdown.
393	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) runCheckAsync(trigger string) {
394		if w.ctx.Err() != nil {
395			return
396		}
397		w.wg.Go(func() {
398			w.checkForChanges(trigger)
399		})
400	}
401	
402	// executePendingCheck executes a pending check if one was scheduled
403	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) executePendingCheck() {
404		w.mu.Lock()
405		defer w.mu.Unlock()
406	
407		if !w.pendingCheck {
408			return
409		}
410	
411		now := time.Now()
412		timeSinceLastCall := now.Sub(w.lastThrottledCall)
413	
414		if timeSinceLastCall >= w.throttleDuration {
415			w.lastThrottledCall = now
416			w.pendingCheck = false
417			w.runCheckAsync("throttled")
418		}
419	}
420	
421	// checkForChanges queries the databases and processes any new or updated sessions.
422	// The checking mutex prevents concurrent executions that would multiply DB connections.
423	func (w *CursorIDEWatcher) checkForChanges(trigger string) {
424		// Prevent overlapping checks. Normal triggers use TryLock and skip so slow checks
425		// don't pile up goroutines, but the shutdown flush must not be skipped — its whole
426		// purpose is to catch changes an in-flight check's snapshot missed, so it blocks
427		// until that check finishes.
428		if trigger == "shutdown" {
429			w.checking.Lock()
430		} else if !w.checking.TryLock() {
431			slog.Debug("Skipping check, previous check still running", "trigger", trigger)
432			return
433		}
434		defer w.checking.Unlock()
435	
436		slog.Debug("Checking for changes", "trigger", trigger)
437	
438		w.mu.Lock()
439		lastCheck := w.lastCheck
440		w.lastCheck = time.Now()
441		w.mu.Unlock()
442	
443		// Load the project's composer IDs from both association sources: workspace-DB
444		// references (older Cursor) and the workspaceIdentifier embedded in global
445		// composerData rows (the only live source in Cursor >= 3.12).
446		composerIDs, err := FindProjectComposerIDs(w.globalDbPath, w.projectPath, w.workspaces)
447		if err != nil {
448			slog.Error("Failed to load project composer IDs", "error", err)
449			return
450		}
451	
452		if len(composerIDs) == 0 {
453			slog.Debug("No composers found for project")
454			return
455		}
456	
457		// Load composer data from global database
458		composers, err := LoadComposerDataBatch(w.globalDbPath, composerIDs)
459		if err != nil {
460			slog.Error("Failed to load composer data", "error", err)
461			return
462		}
463	
464		// Track new/updated sessions
465		newCount := 0
466		updatedCount := 0
467	
468		for composerID, composer := range composers {
469			// Skip if conversation is empty
470			if len(composer.Conversation) == 0 {
471				continue
472			}
473	
474			// Check if this is a new or updated session
475			w.mu.RLock()
476			knownTimestamp, exists := w.knownComposers[composerID]
477			w.mu.RUnlock()
478	
479			currentTimestamp := composer.LastUpdatedAt
480			if currentTimestamp == 0 {
481				currentTimestamp = composer.CreatedAt
482			}
483	
484			// Determine if we should process this session
485			shouldProcess := false
486			if !exists {
487				// New session
488				shouldProcess = true
489				newCount++
490				slog.Info("Found new session", "composerID", composerID, "name", composer.Name)
491			} else if currentTimestamp > knownTimestamp {
492				// Updated session
493				shouldProcess = true
494				updatedCount++
495				slog.Info("Found updated session",
496					"composerID", composerID,
497					"name", composer.Name,
498					"oldTimestamp", knownTimestamp,
499					"newTimestamp", currentTimestamp)
500			}
501	
502			if shouldProcess {
503				// Guard against a race condition: Cursor may commit the composerData record
504				// (updating LastUpdatedAt and FullConversationHeadersOnly) before the
505				// corresponding bubble records are committed to the database. If the header
506				// list references more bubbles than were actually loaded, the session data is
507				// incomplete. By not advancing knownComposers, the next check cycle will
508				// re-process this session once all bubbles are available.
509				if len(composer.FullConversationHeadersOnly) > 0 &&
510					len(composer.Conversation) < len(composer.FullConversationHeadersOnly) {
511					// Debug, not Warn: this is expected, transient state while Cursor is
512					// mid-write, and it fires routinely during normal streaming.
513					slog.Debug("Incomplete composer data (bubble records not yet committed), will retry on next check",
514						"composerID", composerID,
515						"expectedBubbles", len(composer.FullConversationHeadersOnly),
516						"loadedBubbles", len(composer.Conversation))
517					continue
518				}
519	
520				// Guard against a second race condition: the bubble count may match the header
521				// count (so the guard above passes), but the last committed bubble is a user
522				// message with no agent response yet. This happens because Cursor writes the
523				// user bubble and updates lastUpdatedAt in one step, before the agent has
524				// produced a reply. Processing now would generate markdown that is missing the
525				// agent response entirely.
526				//
527				// We skip the session and let knownComposers stay at the old timestamp so it
528				// is re-evaluated on the next check cycle (when the agent reply arrives).
529				// The pendingIncomplete map records when we first saw the session in this
530				// state. If the agent never replies (e.g. the user abandoned the chat),
531				// we process the session anyway after incompleteTimeout so the markdown is
532				// not lost permanently.
533				if len(composer.Conversation) > 0 {
534					lastBubble := &composer.Conversation[len(composer.Conversation)-1]
535					if lastBubble.Type == 1 {
536						w.mu.Lock()
537						firstSeen, alreadyPending := w.pendingIncomplete[composerID]
538						if !alreadyPending {
539							w.pendingIncomplete[composerID] = time.Now()
540							w.mu.Unlock()
541							// Debug, not Warn: waiting for the agent reply is the normal
542							// state while the user's request is in flight.
543							slog.Debug("Last bubble is a user message (agent not yet responded), will retry on next check",
544								"composerID", composerID,
545								"lastBubbleID", lastBubble.BubbleID)
546							continue
547						}
548						if time.Since(firstSeen) < w.incompleteTimeout {
549							w.mu.Unlock()
550							slog.Debug("Still waiting for agent response, will retry on next check",
551								"composerID", composerID,
552								"waited", time.Since(firstSeen))
553							continue
554						}
555						// Timed out — the agent likely never replied; process anyway.
556						delete(w.pendingIncomplete, composerID)
557						w.mu.Unlock()
558						slog.Warn("Timed out waiting for agent response, processing incomplete session",
559							"composerID", composerID,
560							"waited", time.Since(firstSeen))
561					} else {
562						// Last bubble is an agent message — clear any stale pending state.
563						w.mu.Lock()
564						delete(w.pendingIncomplete, composerID)
565						w.mu.Unlock()
566					}
567				}
568	
569				// Convert to AgentChatSession
570				session, err := ConvertToAgentChatSession(composer, w.projectPath)
571				if err != nil {
572					// Don't advance knownComposers on failure — leave the watermark where it
573					// was so this composer is retried on the next check instead of being
574					// silently skipped forever.
575					slog.Warn("Failed to convert composer to session",
576						"composerID", composerID,
577						"error", err)
578					continue
579				}
580	
581				// Update known timestamp. Only done after a successful conversion so a
582				// failure (see above) doesn't permanently poison the watermark for this composer.
583				w.mu.Lock()
584				w.knownComposers[composerID] = currentTimestamp
585				w.mu.Unlock()
586	
587				// Write debug output if requested
588				if w.debugRaw {
589					if err := writeDebugOutput(session); err != nil {
590						slog.Warn("Failed to write debug output",
591							"sessionID", session.SessionID,
592							"error", err)
593					}
594				}
595	
596				// Invoke callback asynchronously so a panic during processing (e.g. markdown
597				// write or cloud sync) doesn't crash the watcher, and slow callback I/O
598				// doesn't delay processing of the remaining sessions in this check.
599				slog.Info("Invoking callback for session",
600					"sessionID", session.SessionID,
601					"slug", session.Slug)
602				w.callbackWg.Go(func() {
603					defer func() {
604						if r := recover(); r != nil {
605							slog.Error("Session callback panicked", "panic", r, "sessionID", session.SessionID)
606						}
607					}()
608					w.sessionCallback(session)
609				})
610			}
611		}
612	
613		// On the very first check lastCheck is the zero time; report 0 instead of a
614		// nonsensical ~2000-year duration.
615		var elapsed time.Duration
616		if !lastCheck.IsZero() {
617			elapsed = time.Since(lastCheck)
618		}
619		slog.Info("Completed check for changes",
620			"trigger", trigger,
621			"totalComposers", len(composers),
622			"newSessions", newCount,
623			"updatedSessions", updatedCount,
624			"elapsedSinceLastCheck", elapsed)
625	}
```

```text
5	// DispatchSession hands session to cb on its own goroutine, recovering from a
6	// panic so that one malformed session cannot take down a running watcher.
7	// label names the provider in the panic log.
8	//
9	// Delivery is fire-and-forget: a watcher that must wait for in-flight callbacks
10	// before shutting down needs its own WaitGroup around cb instead.
11	func DispatchSession(label string, cb func(*AgentChatSession), session *AgentChatSession) {
12		if cb == nil || session == nil {
13			return
14		}
15		go DeliverSession(label, cb, session)
16	}
17	
18	// DeliverSession invokes a callback synchronously and contains consumer panics.
19	// Watchers with one worker use it to preserve ordering and join all saves before
20	// returning an agent's exit status.
21	func DeliverSession(label string, cb func(*AgentChatSession), session *AgentChatSession) {
22		if cb == nil || session == nil {
23			return
24		}
25		defer func() {
26			if r := recover(); r != nil {
27				slog.Error(label+": session callback panicked", "panic", r)
28			}
29		}()
30		cb(session)
31	}
```

```text
// performing case-insensitive matching to find the correct casing on disk.
// This ensures that the returned path matches the real filesystem casing, which is
// important for consistent hashing and avoiding subtle bugs on case-insensitive filesystems.
//
// Note: This can be slow for long paths or directories with many entries, since it
// requires reading each directory's contents.
//
// If a component doesn't exist on disk, the remaining path components are
// appended as-is, making this function safe to use with paths that don't
// fully exist yet.
func GetCanonicalPath(p string) (string, error) {
	// Ensure we have an absolute, clean path
	p = filepath.Clean(p)
	if !filepath.IsAbs(p) {
		var err error
		p, err = filepath.Abs(p)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
	}

	// Resolve any symlinks in the path to get the real physical path
	// This is critical for ensuring consistent path hashing across different
	// ways of accessing the same directory (e.g., through a symlink vs directly)
	realPath, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(p)
	if err == nil && realPath != p {
		// Successfully resolved symlinks - update p to the resolved path for case normalization
		p = realPath
	} else if err != nil {
		// Symlink resolution failed (e.g., path doesn't exist yet, or Windows junction points).
		// This is expected in normal operation — fall back to the original path and continue
		// with case normalization below.
		slog.Debug("GetCanonicalPath: symlink resolution failed, using original path",
			"path", p, "error", err)
	}

	// Separate the volume (drive letter "D:" or UNC share "\\server\share" on Windows,
	// empty on Unix) from the rest of the path. Without this, splitting "D:\foo\bar" on
	// the OS separator yields ["D:", "foo", "bar"] — and the original code skipped the
	// first element under the assumption it was empty (true only for Unix paths like
	// "/foo/bar"). The drive letter would be silently dropped, leaving a path that
	// resolved against the current drive instead of the requested one. UNC paths were
	// even worse: "\\server\share\foo" would lose one of the leading backslashes and
	// stop being a UNC reference at all.
	volume := filepath.VolumeName(p)
	remainder := p[len(volume):]

	// Split the remainder. The leading separator produces an empty first element which
	// we skip, so on every platform the loop processes only real path components.
	parts := strings.Split(remainder, string(os.PathSeparator))

	// Walk from the volume root. On Unix that's "/"; on Windows it's "D:\" or
	// "\\server\share\".
	result := volume + string(os.PathSeparator)

	firstPartIndex := 1

	// Build path component by component
	for i := firstPartIndex; i < len(parts); i++ {
		if parts[i] == "" {
			continue
		}

		// Open current result directory to read its contents
		f, err := os.Open(result)
		if err != nil {
			// Can't read directory - might not exist yet
			// Append remaining path as-is
			return appendRemainingParts(result, parts, i), nil
		}

		names, err := f.Readdirnames(-1)
		_ = f.Close() // Best effort close, error doesn't affect result
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}

		// Find the correct case
		found := false
		for _, name := range names {
			if strings.EqualFold(name, parts[i]) {
				result = filepath.Join(result, name)
				found = true
				break
			}
		}

		if !found {
			// Component doesn't exist, append remaining as-is
			result = appendRemainingParts(result, parts, i)
			break
		}
	}

	return result, nil
}

// CanonicalizePathOrClean resolves path to the canonical form used for
// comparing paths recorded by an agent against paths seen locally, and returns
// "" for blank input.
//
// Unlike GetCanonicalPath it never fails: a path that cannot be canonicalized
// (most often because it was recorded on another machine and does not exist
// here) still needs to compare equal to itself, so it degrades to a cleaned
// absolute path and finally to a plain Clean.
func CanonicalizePathOrClean(path string) string {
	trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(path)
	if trimmed == "" {
		return ""
	}
	if canonical, err := GetCanonicalPath(trimmed); err == nil {
		return canonical
	}
	if abs, err := filepath.Abs(trimmed); err == nil {
		return filepath.Clean(abs)
	}
	return filepath.Clean(trimmed)
}

// debugBaseDirOverride allows overriding the base directory for debug output.
// When set, debug files are written to this directory instead of the default
// .specstory/debug/ location. This is set via the --debug-dir CLI flag or
// the debug_dir config option.
var debugBaseDirOverride string

// SetDebugBaseDir sets the override base directory for debug output.
// When set to a non-empty value, GetDebugDir will use this as the base
// When set, debug files are written to this directory instead of the default

var debugBaseDirOverride string
// SetDebugBaseDir sets the override base directory for debug output.
// When set to a non-empty value, GetDebugDir will use this as the base
// instead of the default .specstory/debug/ path.
func SetDebugBaseDir(dir string) {

// GetDebugDir returns the debug directory path for a given session ID or UUID.
//
// The debug directory is used to store detailed JSON records and debugging
// information for SpecStory CLI sessions. This is shared across all providers
// (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor CLI) to maintain a consistent debug structure.
//
// When debugBaseDirOverride is set (via SetDebugBaseDir), the directory structure
// is: <override>/<sessionID>/
// Otherwise: .specstory/debug/<sessionID>/
//
// Example:
//
//	debugDir := spi.GetDebugDir("abc123-def456")
//	// Returns: ".specstory/debug/abc123-def456"
func GetDebugDir(sessionID string) string {
	if debugBaseDirOverride != "" {
		return filepath.Join(debugBaseDirOverride, sessionID)
	}
	return filepath.Join(".specstory", "debug", sessionID)
}
var numberedDebugFileRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^[1-9][0-9]*\.json$`)
// IsNumberedDebugFile identifies the files owned by a numbered debug export.
func IsNumberedDebugFile(name string) bool {
	return numberedDebugFileRe.MatchString(name)
}
// PrepareDebugDir clears only provider-owned files before refreshing an export.
// CLI artifacts such as session-data.json and unrelated files must survive.
func PrepareDebugDir(dir string, ownsFile func(string) bool) error {
	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("create debug directory %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("read debug directory %s: %w", dir, err)
	}
	for _, entry := range entries {
		if entry.IsDir() || !ownsFile(entry.Name()) {
			continue
		}
		path := filepath.Join(dir, entry.Name())
		if err := os.Remove(path); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("remove debug file %s: %w", path, err)
		}
	}
	return nil
}
// WriteDebugRecords refreshes numbered, pretty-printed records from a parsing
// snapshot. Pass json.RawMessage when native bytes are available to preserve
// unknown fields, numeric precision, and key order; typed diagnostics also use
// this writer so numbering, cleanup, formatting, and errors stay consistent.
func WriteDebugRecords[T any](dir string, records []T) error {
	if err := PrepareDebugDir(dir, IsNumberedDebugFile); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for i, record := range records {
		path := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("%d.json", i+1))
		data, err := json.MarshalIndent(record, "", "  ")
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("format debug file %s: %w", path, err)
		}
		if err := os.WriteFile(path, data, 0o644); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("write debug file %s: %w", path, err)
		}
	}
	return nil
}
// WriteDebugJSONL exports an already accepted JSONL snapshot without decoding
// records through float64 or rereading the source file during a live update.
func WriteDebugJSONL(dir, transcript string) error {
	var records []json.RawMessage
	for line := range strings.SplitSeq(transcript, "\n") {
		if strings.TrimSpace(line) != "" {
			records = append(records, json.RawMessage(line))
		}
	}
	return WriteDebugRecords(dir, records)
}
// WriteDebugSessionData writes the SessionData as formatted JSON to the debug directory.
// This provides a standardized, provider-agnostic debug output alongside provider-specific raw data.
//
// The file is written to: .specstory/debug/<sessionID>/session-data.json
//
// Returns an error if the debug directory cannot be created or the file cannot be written.
func WriteDebugSessionData(sessionID string, sessionData *schema.SessionData) error {
	if sessionData == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("sessionData is nil")
	}
	// Get debug directory
	debugDir := GetDebugDir(sessionID)
	// Create debug directory if it doesn't exist
	if err := os.MkdirAll(debugDir, 0755); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to create debug directory: %w", err)
	}
	// Marshal SessionData to pretty-printed JSON
	jsonData, err := json.MarshalIndent(sessionData, "", "  ")
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal SessionData: %w", err)
	}
	// Write to session-data.json
	filePath := filepath.Join(debugDir, "session-data.json")
	if err := os.WriteFile(filePath, jsonData, 0644); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("failed to write session-data.json: %w", err)
	}
	// Log absolute path for debugging
	absPath, _ := filepath.Abs(filePath)
	slog.Debug("Wrote debug session data", "sessionId", sessionID, "path", absPath)
	return nil
}
```
